title: Eva Jessye, his first real music teacher
summary: Eva Jessye teaches him piano and voice in Taft, later becomes Dr. Eva Jessye with her own choir, and visits him at the Apollo.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So anyway, as things went on, a young lady, Eva Jessye, was the first to ever teach me--besides my sister--on the piano. She was one of the teachers, and she was a vocal teacher, and she went on a little later to fame. She left Taft and came to New York and worked and had the Eva Jessye Choir, and now she's known as Dr. Eva Jessye. As of right now, I tried to contact her to get some points before I came up here, she's in some capacity at the University of Kansas--Kansas State College in Pittsburgh. She's now, I think, eighty something years old.
And that was my first real music teacher. And I don't know why she thought that I should sing, but in some ways, during her

training, my voice was changing, and it looked like I couldn't get things right, and I just dwelled in myself, that oh, I can't sing. And so we laughed about that later on after I met her, because she left the area and went on for years and years, and then I went to travel as a band.
She came to see me, my first trip at the Apollo Theatre in New York City, and she was saying how nice it was, but why wasn't I singing something. And I told her I never could sing.
